question: Does a fourth seat in the two demand peaks satisfy the low-risk guardrail at fewer paid seat-hours than a continuous fourth seat?
boundary_rule: Repeat daily. A fourth seat can start only at left-inclusive, right-exclusive times; it finishes its active service without preemption. At simultaneous availability prefer the lowest regular seat ID, then the fourth seat.
baseline_secondary: B only: report P(W_L>60 | L arrives in [13:00,14:00)) and the corresponding [21:00,22:00) arrival cohort for the scheduled vs fixed-four A20 plans. If the B scheduled A20 guardrail is met, replay the same root/IDs on the same shifts with FCFS and estimate A20-minus-FCFS signed H and L contrasts; at least 2 pp H reduction is the original practical benchmark.
units: H/L within-class fractions per replication, reported as % levels and pp differences; paid seat-hours per 24-hour day for staffing. Three permanent seats cost 72 seat-hours/day before the additional seat.
paid_definition: All scheduled hours including idle time, plus only the actual fourth-seat busy time outside all its scheduled windows. All terms are intersected with the measurement period before division by measured days; no monetary or overtime-premium model.
inference: Each plan replays the exact same alert-ID table within its environment and replication. Pointwise two-sided Student t intervals on 100 levels or within-replication differences, never pooled across environments. Upper 95% endpoint <=5% meets L guardrail; lower >5% exceeds; otherwise uncertain. No noninferiority or equivalence threshold assumed. No search over staffing windows, no optional stopping.
